title: TLXML: Task-Level Explanation of Meta-Learning via Influence Functions
abstract: arXiv:2501.14271v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Meta-learning enables models to rapidly adapt to new tasks by leveraging prior experience, but its adaptation mechanisms remain opaque, especially regarding how past training tasks influence future predictions. We introduce TLXML (Task-Level eXplanation of Meta-Learning), a novel framework that extends influence functions to meta-learning settings and provides task-level explanations of adaptation and inference. By reformulating influence functions for the bi-level structure of meta-learning, we quantify the contribution of each meta-training task to the adapted model's behaviour. To ensure scalability, we propose a Gauss-Newton-based approximation that significantly reduces computational complexity from $O(pq^2)$ to $O(pq)$, where $p$ and $q$ denote the numbers of model and meta parameters, respectively. translated_title: TLXML：通过影响函数实现元学习的任务级解释
translated_abstract: 元学习使模型能够通过利用先前经验快速适应新任务，但其适应机制仍不透明，尤其是在过去训练任务如何影响未来预测方面。我们引入了TLXML（元学习的任务级解释），这是一种新颖的框架，将影响函数扩展到元学习设置中，并提供适应和推理的任务级解释。通过为元学习的双层结构重新制定影响函数，我们量化了每个元训练任务对适应模型行为的贡献。为确保可扩展性，我们提出了一种基于高斯-牛顿的近似方法，将计算复杂度从$O(pq^2)$显著降低到$O(pq)$，其中$p$和$q$分别表示模型参数和元参数的数量。此外，我们提出了使用伪逆Hessian定义的广义影响函数，即使当损失函数不可逆或奇异时也能适用。
tldr: 本文提出TLXML框架，通过扩展影响函数到元学习，并采用高斯-牛顿近似降低计算复杂度，从而提供任务级解释，揭示元训练任务对模型适应行为的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TLXML, a framework extending influence functions to meta-learning with a Gauss-Newton approximation to reduce computational complexity, enabling task-level explanations of how meta-training tasks affect model adaptation.
